name: Shiyi Wei
description: Shiyi Wei is a PhD student in theoretical physics at Université Côte d’Azur and INPHYNI, working on quantum diffusion, nonequilibrium transport and fluctuations.
bio: I am a PhD student in theoretical physics at Université Côte d’Azur, based at the Institut de Physique de Nice (INPHYNI). I started my PhD in November 2024, supervised by Mathias Albert with Tony Jin as co-supervisor.

My research concerns quantum diffusion and nonequilibrium transport, with particular interest in fluctuations, disorder and macroscopic fluctuation theory. I study how density and current fluctuations in noisy quantum systems connect with classical stochastic processes.

Before my PhD, I studied physics at École Normale Supérieure in Paris, including the ICFP master's programme in the Quantum Physics track. I previously studied mathematics and physics at Sorbonne Université.
interests: Nonequilibrium statistical physics and disordered systems
Density and current fluctuations in noisy quantum systems
Large deviations and macroscopic fluctuation theory

paragraphs: I compete in table tennis for Nice Cavigal Tennis de Table (licence no. 7527003). I have also recently taken up road cycling.

details: Initial thesis project: Towards a typical theory of quantum diffusion.
Master 1 and Master 2 ICFP, Quantum Physics track.

education.degree: Licence 1 and 2, Mathematics and Physics (double major)

research_experience.description: Theoretical study and analytical and numerical modelling of fluctuations in nonequilibrium disordered systems.
Analytical calculation of nonequilibrium current cumulants in the quantum symmetric simple exclusion process (QSSEP), using the Lindblad formalism and quantum Itô calculus.
Modelled a Tonks–Girardeau gas and numerically simulated its density matrix in Mathematica.
Studied quantum-state reconstruction using Wigner distributions, coherent states and quantum squeezing.
